comments:
The misalignment is actually useful (and, I'd argue, not messed up):

The first set of items you see (e.g. act, `allure`, `aom`, `gettext`)  are formulae. The second set set of items (e.g. `android-studio`, `appolice`, `font-meslolg-nerd-font`) are casks.

They happen to be aligned differently because the alignment is set differently within each group. Delineating the two sets with a header that says `Formulae:` for the first set and `Casks:` for the second might be useful here.

Not really sure what you mean by a "non-cask formula", though. A formula isn't a cask, so all formulae are non-casks.

> The misalignment is actually useful (and, I'd argue, not messed up):

agreed 👍🏻

@carlocab I understand your argument above and thank you for the PR you submitted, which will indeed make it much less confusing. As for the `messed up`, I stand by it: try `brew ls` when your terminal uses 2 spaces for tabs (`tabs -2`). Nothing is aligned. Here is a screenshot so that things aren't fixed by GitHub defaulting to 8 spaces per tab: Relying on tabs (of unknown width) for padding doesn't work, formulaes should use space characters like casks do. Looking at the code, I realize it's an artifact of delegating to different commands (`ls` vs `find`). Maybe some filtering of the output to replace tabs with 8 spaces would fix it?

What does the output of `ls $(brew --cellar)` look like?

If the output of `ls` is also messed up, then I'm not sure monkey-patching the output of `ls` to get it to come out right in non-standard setups is the correct move for `brew`. This probably needs to be fixed in `ls`, not in `brew`.

If the output isn't, then we can look into why `brew` is breaking `ls`' output.

**Edit:** Tried this myself, and the problem is with `ls`. This will need to be fixed there.

> I stand by it: try `brew ls` when your terminal uses 2 spaces for tabs (`tabs -2`).

Don't do that then. This behaviour has been the case the entire time `brew ls` has existed as a command.

As @carlocab points out: your issue is with `ls` (which we shell out to).

You're right, I thought maybe brew was not invoking ls properly but when I try the default BSD `ls` in my terminal it's the same misaligned thing 😢  (I've always aliased `ls` to `gls` so it's never been an issue for me).

review_comments: I wonder if we should deprecate these `ls_args` if we're not going to do them for casks?
I find these `ls_args` kinda useful, and I'm not sure they have a clear analogue for casks. Though I suppose you can get them and more by using `ls` in `HOMEBREW_CELLAR`.
Are those flags as useful when applied to `/usr/local/Caskroom` as they are for `HOMEBREW_CELLAR`? Genuine question; I actually don't know. I'll look into it.
They look equally useful applied to either to me. I'd argue using a consistent method of outputting both would be good (i.e. `ls` for both or neither)
Ok, I think I'm happy to use `ls` for both then. I'll do that in a follow-up PR so we can get adequate feedback from Cask maintainers.
